name: Nuclei
description: Version client sets InsecureSkipVerify:true; -update SHA256 skipped if checksums.txt absent; templates auto-fetched every run with ZERO verification.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Nuclei exposes separate engine and template update controls. Its template manager updates an existing template directory only when version state requires it, using a GitHub release downloader; the reviewed source places InsecureSkipVerify in the headless browser client, so that setting should not be attributed to the update channel. The release downloader's end-to-end artifact verification remains unresolved from this snapshot.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than historical release re-verification; the delegated github release downloader and binary updater implementation were not audited here, so artifact verification and version-channel TLS behavior remain unresolved.

original_evidence.text: | Nuclei | github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei | Go — binary self-update (`-update`/`-up`) **and** a separate automatic nuclei-templates channel | Y — two distinct channels (see auto column) | **Binary**: chk automatic every run (via pdtm API), but dl/inst strictly **manual** (`-update`/`-up` flag required). **Templates**: chk **and** dl/inst are **automatic by default on every single run** (`FreshInstallIfNotExists` + `UpdateIfOutdated` called unconditionally in `runner.New()`) unless disabled via `-duc`/`CanCheckForUpdates()` | Y — **templates**: downloaded YAML is loaded directly into the scan engine and drives execution (including protocols capable of running commands when such templates/flags are enabled), so a compromised template feed = executed scan logic, and this happens automatically with no user action. **Binary**: downloaded archive directly replaces the running executable via `github.com/minio/selfupdate.Apply()` (manual trigger only) | https — GitHub REST API via `go-github` client + signed asset redirect URLs (normal TLS cert validation) for both binary and template downloads. **However**, the separate `api.pdtm.sh` version-check/ignore-file client explicitly sets `TLSClientConfig{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` — TLS certificate validation is **disabled** for that channel | no — `checksums.txt` is just another unsigned GitHub release asset from the same repo/trust boundary; no GPG/cosign/code-signing anywhere (explicit TODO in source) | **Binary self-update**: hash-from-manifest, SHA-256 checked against a `checksums.txt` release asset — but **soft-fail**: if that asset is missing from the release, verification is silently skipped entirely (`expectedChecksum` stays empty ⇒ compare branch never runs). **Templates (automatic channel)**: **none** — `DownloadSourceWithCallback` unpacks the GitHub source zipball straight to disk with zero checksum/signature check; the local `.checksum` (MD5) file is computed *after the fact* from files already on disk purely to print a change-summary table, not to verify anything against a trusted value | none — TODO comment in source states code-signing verification ("selfupdate...has support for checksum validation, code signing verification etc. implement them after discussion") is **not implemented** | `pkg/installer/versioncheck.go:17-23,37-121` (pdtm API version check);
